page: Amazon Web Services m8g.24xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, includes a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, and does not feature local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving top-tier status across both cached small-block reads and large-block uncached read and write operations. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core performance and gzip single-threaded compression scoring in the middle 50%. In LLM inference tests, the instance exhibits a notable tradeoff: while text generation for medium and large models ranks in the top 10%, text generation for small models falls into the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8g.24xlarge offers high resource density and strong multi-core throughput relative to its arm64 hardware profile, making it a viable option for highly parallelized workloads without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. The instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-to-large scale LLM text generation.
